newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks finish lower, weak undertone.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks finish lower, weak undertone.

text.p: Shares erased early morning gains to end with losses at Bombay bourses on Monday as a negative sentiment weighed heavy on minds of market players, traders said.
"It was a pretty bad day. Overall, sentiment continues to be bearish," said Dheeraj Agarwal, trader at SS Kantilal Ishwarlal Securities, a local brokerage.
Dealers said new rules on short selling announced by market regulator the Securities & Exchange Board of India(SEBI) limited trading volumes and kept major players to the sidelines.
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) top index fell 38.65 points, or 1.34 percent, to end at a provisional 2,851.85.
Issued by SEBI last Thursday, the rules to be effective this week require all exchanges to ask member-brokers to submit their scrip-wise net short sales positions at the end of the day.
Market players said the latest move by the regulator will not do much to revive the sagging bourses, with volumes cited as the first casualty of the short-selling rules.
"It'll lead to lower volumes...Whenever the government has made any restrictions, the market has gone down," said dealer Zubin Tampal at brokers Motilal Oswal said.
Trader Ramnik Parikh said, "Volumes will come down because of the new restrictions."
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) said it imposed a sale price limit (circuit breaker) on Gujarat Ambuja Cement after the stock broke the weekly 15 percent range at the NSE.
The limit was set at 230.90 rupees. At the BSE, the stock lost 13.50 rupees to end at 202.75 in volumes of 580.010 shares.
Traders said foreign funds and speculators were sellers in auto stocks on fears of a prolonged economic slowdown.
Bajaj Auto fell 51.10 rupees to 793.0, M&M 14.75 to 274.50, TELCO 22.50 to 294.0, SBI 1.75 to 216.50, TISCO 0.50 to 152.75, ITC 4.25 to 275.50, ACC 37.70 to 965 and Reliance 0.25 to 180.5.
